The Colorado River crisis is a direct result of decades of bureaucratic mismanagement and outdated allocation formulas. While Dina Titus frames this as a "wake-up call," the real issue is Washington's failure to modernize water rights for the 21st century. The Quantification Settlement Agreement locked San Diego into dependency while ignoring evolving climate realities—classic D.C. short-term thinking.

Trump's America First approach demands actual solutions: renegotiate the 1922 Compact's obsolete quotas, slash agricultural subsidies for water-intensive crops in deserts, and deploy modular nuclear reactors to power desalination plants. Conservation theater won't fix structural over-allocation. The Lower Basin's 20% cuts proposal? Too little. Lake Mead's dead pool scenario requires immediate 40% reductions basin-wide. Prioritize cities over alfalfa fields. Audit every federal dollar spent on "drought resilience" programs that fund more studies than pipes.

Real leadership means forcing Phoenix and LA to recycle 90% of wastewater—like Singapore—instead of begging rural users to sacrifice. The era of pretending there's enough water for 50 million people in a desert is over. Time for hard choices, not more committee meetings.
